_note: Recorded from the real local backend (Phase 4B, 2026-10-25): GET /api/v1/traces/{id}/diagnostics?project=1 (contract llminsight.diagnostics.v1) for the retry and nested fixture traces. SYNTHETIC telemetry. Contract fixture only; contains no credential.

limitations.text: Only spans stored at the time of this request are analysed; spans exported later, dropped by an exporter or rejected by the ingest are not visible.
Only stored, allowlisted metadata is used. Prompts, completions and error descriptions are never stored (ADR-19, R21) and were not used.
The telemetry is labelled SYNTHETIC: findings describe test or mock traffic, not observed behaviour of a real provider.

findings.trigger: A logical call (one llminsight.call_id) has at least one inference attempt with span status ERROR, and its highest-numbered stored attempt does not have span status ERROR.

hypothesis.statement: Possible explanation (not verified): the condition behind the failed attempt(s) was transient and had cleared by the retried attempt.

error_interpretation.statement: The recorded error.type is HTTP 429 (too many requests) or openai.RateLimitError: this suggests the provider or an intermediary throttled these attempts. The stored data does not show which limit applied.

established: At least one attempt of this logical call failed and a later attempt completed without span status ERROR.
A trace has status error whenever any stored span has status ERROR (ARCHITECTURE.md §4.4), so a recovered call alone makes the trace status error (R27).
not_established: Whether the output of the successful attempt was correct or complete: this platform stores no content.
What the application returned to its caller (see the root span status).

limitations.text: Attempts are grouped by llminsight.call_id and llminsight.attempt as asserted by the instrumentation; the server cannot verify them.
error.type is a low-cardinality identifier chosen by the instrumentation; it is not verified against the provider.
The telemetry is labelled SYNTHETIC: findings describe test or mock traffic, not observed behaviour of a real provider.

investigation_steps: Read the recorded error.type of the failed attempt(s) in the evidence.
Check the fact other_error_spans: when it is 0, the trace status error comes only from attempts that were later retried successfully.
Track how often this call needs retries over time (Overview: inference attempts versus logical calls, inference error rate).
Check the provider account's rate and usage limits in the provider's own console (not stored here).

findings.trigger: A usage row has the cost_unknown_reason price_missing.

hypothesis.statement: Possible explanation (not verified): no stored price row matched the attempt's provider and exact model at its start time, or the attempt used a service tier or endpoint the stored prices do not cover (PRICING.md).

established: The cost of these attempts is unknown (NULL), not zero, and excluded from known-cost totals.
No stored price was applied to them at ingest.

limitations.text: The telemetry is labelled SYNTHETIC: findings describe test or mock traffic, not observed behaviour of a real provider.
Unknown values stay unknown: they are never counted as zero tokens or zero cost.

investigation_steps: Compare the recorded response model with the model_prices catalogue.
Check the facts service_tiers and server_addresses: only the standard tier on api.openai.com is priced.
Stored costs are never recomputed: a later catalogue does not change these rows.

not_assessed.reason: No approved comparison basis exists: the contracts define no latency objective or threshold (threshold alerts, M21, are P1), and a percentile of peer attempts would flag a fixed share of attempts by construction. Durations are reported as facts only.
Correctness, relevance and hallucination cannot be assessed from metadata: no prompt or completion is stored (ADR-19) and no evaluation result is linked to this trace.
Prompt content is never stored (ADR-19) and is not reconstructed.
One trace cannot establish a provider-wide incident, and no provider status data is stored.
Findings are hypotheses; a root-cause decision needs human review (Failure Review, ADR-10).
